title: MIT Frame Packer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: CAN Motor Control for Robotics
description: Set the position, speed, Kp, Kd and torque of an MIT-mode command for a Damiao motor and see each value become a whole number, its hexadecimal form and the eight bytes of the CAN frame. Then work out the whole number yourself in six problems. Used in Chapter 9.

educational.topic: Packing an MIT-mode command into a CAN frame
learningObjectives: Calculate the whole number that a value becomes when it is packed into an MIT-mode field of a Damiao motor, in six problems, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Watch five values become integers and bytes, then carry out the formula by hand on new values with the working shown after each answer
keyQuestions: Why does a speed of 0 not pack to exactly the middle number?
Why do Kp and Kd use a different range from the torque?
commonMisconceptions: A value of zero maps to the middle number exactly
All the fields have the same range
The conversion rounds to the nearest whole number
assessmentOpportunities: Six typed whole numbers, one attempt each; 5 of 6 for mastery

controls.label: Speed
controls.range: plus or minus the model's limit in rad/s, step 0.1, default 0.0

controls.label: Torque
controls.range: plus or minus the model's limit in N·m, step 0.1, default 0.0

controls.label: Your answer
controls.range: a whole number from 0 to 2^bits - 1, no default
